Summary Former Communications and Multimedia Deputy Minister Datuk Zahidi Zainul Abidin passed away and was buried at Bayan Lepas Islamic Cemetery after Isyak prayers.
 His death was confirmed by his brother, who said Zahidi, aged 65, suffered from kidney failure and was receiving treatment in Penang.
 Zahidi served as Padang Besar MP for two terms and held key roles, including Deputy Minister under the PN and BN administrations.

 Subscribe GEORGE TOWN, Nov 14 — Former Communications and Multimedia deputy minister Datuk Zahidi Zainul Abidin died yesterday and was laid to rest at the Bayan Lepas Islamic Cemetery after Isyak prayers last night.
 News of his passing was shared by former Perlis Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Shahidan Kassim, who extended his condolences to the deceased’s family.
 In a Facebook post, Shahidan, who is the Member of Parliament for Arau, said he was deeply saddened by his friend’s passing.
 “It is with sadness that I inform you of the passing of the former Padang Besar Member of Parliament, a man who had rendered invaluable service. His passing is a great loss to us all.
 “Innalillahi wa inna ilaihi raji’un. Throughout his life, he had dedicated himself to the people of Padang Besar. May Allah SWT forgive all his sins, accept his good deeds and sacrifices, and place his soul among the righteous,” Shahidan said in the post.
 Earlier, a condolence poster announcing Zahidi’s death went viral on social media, accompanied by details of the funeral prayer and burial arrangements, which were held at Masjid Bayan Lepas.
 The news was subsequently confirmed by the deceased’s younger brother, Zafruddin Zainul Abidin. Zafruddin said his elder brother died at about 5pm yesterday.
 He was reported to have said that he had been informed of his brother’s deteriorating health since Wednesday and that Zahidi had been receiving treatment at a private hospital in Penang. He was believed to have been suffering from kidney failure and required dialysis.
 Zahidi, 65, served as the Padang Besar Member of Parliament for two terms after winning the seat in the 13th and 14th General Elections.
 He held several key positions in national politics and administration, including Deputy Communications and Multimedia Minister under the Perikatan Nasional (PN) and Barisan Nasional (BN) administrations from March 2020 to November 2022.
 In Perlis politics, he served as a state executive councillor from 1999 to 2006 during Shahidan’s tenure as Menteri Besar. He was also the Beseri state assemblyman from 1999 to 2008. — Bernama
